comments.author: @tysoncung
comments.text: The part that got me: Kenya's line was meant to reach Uganda, but the last 273 kilometres to Malaba still do not exist. Chinese lenders balked, and a Turkish contractor is only now surveying the route. Meanwhile Ethiopia's electrified line runs all 759 kilometres to Djibouti and turns a three day road trip into twelve hours. Sources are in the description. If a new railway opened near you, did it actually change how you travel, or does it still stop short of where you need to go?
